claim.statement: Between 29 April and 1 May 2026, Tehran's water authorities and Persian reporting converged on a euphemistic rationing pattern: officials denied formal cutoffs or rationing while saying pressure would be reduced from around midnight until morning to reduce leakage and refill urban reservoirs, and Ettelaat/Vista reported noticeable overnight pressure reduction across all Tehran neighborhoods.
claim.subject: Tehran water network
claim.object: de facto nighttime rationing by pressure control

evidence.summary: Akharin Khabar/Tasnim quoted the water-industry spokesman saying Tehran pressure is reduced from about midnight to near morning to reduce leaks and refill urban reservoirs.
Ettelaat/Vista reported that pressure in all Tehran neighborhoods had been noticeably reduced overnight for water-resource management and reservoir refilling.
Earlier KNB v1 source already stored the May 1 overnight-pressure reduction report.

information_depth.rationale: The pattern is supported by official spokesman language and multiple Persian reports; the main uncertainty is neighborhood-level severity.

claim.statement: By 30 April-1 May 2026, Persian water reporting put Tehran's supply margin in emergency territory: Tehran dams were described as 9 percent full with Taleghan and 3 percent without Taleghan, while Karaj dam storage was reported around 14 million cubic meters, enough for roughly two weeks of Tehran drinking water.
claim.subject: Tehran water supply system
claim.object: single-digit dam storage and a roughly two-week Karaj margin

evidence.summary: Didban Iran/Vista quoted Tehran Water and Wastewater's manager saying national dam average was 32 percent while Tehran dams were 9 percent with Taleghan and 3 percent without Taleghan.
EcoIran/Vista reported Karaj dam storage at 14 million cubic meters, enough for about two weeks of Tehran drinking water.

information_depth.rationale: The sources provide concrete percentages and volume/time-margin figures tied to named reservoirs.

assessment.uncertainty: Reservoir percentages shifted across outlets as inflows changed; follow-up should track direct water-company numbers, not only aggregator headlines.

claim.statement: On 30 April 2026, Shahrara/Vista reported that the four dams supplying Mashhad's drinking water held only 6 percent of capacity and were 94 percent empty, while officials still said there was currently no water-rationing plan for the city.
claim.subject: Mashhad drinking-water dams

evidence.summary: Shahrara/Vista reported that Doosti, Torogh, Kardeh, and Ardak dams had 6 percent water and 94 percent empty storage, with officials saying there was no current rationing plan.

information_depth.rationale: The storage and no-rationing figures are explicit, but direct regional water-company confirmation would improve reliability.

claim.statement: By 29-30 April 2026, industrial electricity policy had a visible May 10 cliff: the Energy Ministry said industries could use full electricity until 20 Ordibehesht 1405, after which continuation would be decided weekly by temperature, consumption, and production, while Ettelaat-linked commentary said quotaing industrial electricity from that date would threaten employment and national security.
claim.subject: Iranian industrial electricity supply

evidence.summary: Iran Online/IRNA quoted Deputy Energy Minister Rajabi Mashhadi saying industries have full electricity until 20 Ordibehesht and that continuation is decided weekly based on temperature, consumption, and production.

Roozno's reproduction of Ettelaat's warning said the Ministry of Energy had decided to quota industry electricity from 20 Ordibehesht and argued industrial cutoffs are more dangerous than temporary household blackouts.
The prior KNB source stores the Iran Online official statement on full industrial electricity until 20 Ordibehesht.

information_depth.rationale: Official and semi-official Persian sources identify the same date and mechanism, while differing in whether the tone is reassurance or warning.

assessment.uncertainty: This establishes the policy risk date, not actual post-May-10 delivered electricity.

claim.statement: Late-April to 1 May 2026 Persian electricity reporting combined resilience messaging with fragility signals: Shargh described roughly 60,000 billion toman of war damage to the grid, around 2,000 affected network areas and 6,473 damaged equipment/line/substation points, and officials simultaneously asked households to cut electricity use ahead of a hotter, drier summer.
claim.subject: Iranian electricity grid
claim.object: large war-damage claims, stability messaging, and household-saving demands

evidence.summary: Shargh reported about 60,000 billion toman of grid damage, around 2,000 affected network areas, 6,473 damaged points, hot/dry summer risk, and repeated official appeals for public electricity saving.

information_depth.rationale: The figures are detailed but still primarily official-reported; independent engineering assessment is not available in this pass.

claim.statement: The v24 xPool service-stress sample emitted 98 Persian items and was noisy: simple keyword counts found 58 water-related, 42 electricity-related, 12 with direct cut/rationing wording, 12 industry-related, and 6 thunder/lightning false positives; manual inspection found a few direct Tehran/Mashhad water and industrial-electricity grievance posts, but no broad coordinated service-disruption wave.
claim.subject: v24 xPool service-stress sample
claim.object: thin direct service-disruption evidence amid noisy discourse

evidence.summary: The saved xPool dataset emitted 98 items for a Persian water/electricity/rationing/blackout query since 29 April.
Manual and jq inspection counted noisy keyword buckets and found only a few direct service-disruption posts, including Tehran water-cut/pressure complaints and Mashhad water-warning chatter.

information_depth.rationale: The xPool sample is a bounded social sample and useful for signal/noise, not representative population measurement.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v24 - rationing without saying rationing
synthesis.summary: The service-stress layer is now visible in the regime's own vocabulary. Tehran's water system is not being described as formally rationed, but officials and Persian reports say pressure is reduced from midnight to morning to lower leakage and refill reservoirs; local reports put Tehran dams at 9 percent full with Taleghan and 3 percent without, while Karaj dam had only about a two-week margin for Tehran drinking water. Mashhad shows the same denial structure: four drinking-water dams were reported 94 percent empty while officials still said there was no rationing plan. Electricity has a parallel May 10 cliff: industries get full power only until 20 Ordibehesht, then weekly decisions by temperature, consumption, and production, while semi-official commentary warns industrial cutoffs threaten employment and national security. The power grid is also being framed as stable despite tens of thousands of billions of tomans in war damage and thousands of damaged network points, with officials asking households to save before a hot, dry summer. xPool does not yet show a broad social wave around services; it mostly adds scattered ground texture and noise. Net: the crack is not mass service unrest yet, but euphemistic rationing and official consumption discipline moving into ordinary water and power use.
synthesis.limitations: This pass is strong for official and Persian media admissions around pressure management, dam stress, and post-May-10 industrial-power risk. It is weaker for direct lived-service mapping: xPool produced only scattered anecdotes, and several water figures came through Vista aggregations rather than direct water-company pages. Follow-up should revisit May 10 industrial electricity, direct Tehran/Mashhad pressure schedules, and neighborhood-level reports of daytime water cutoffs.

information_depth.rationale: The pass combines official statements, Persian local reporting, existing KNB water/electricity questions, and a bounded social-media noise check.

operations.rationale: The pressure-management pattern is the current bridge between official no-rationing language and household rationing risk.
The 9 percent / 3 percent dam figures and Karaj two-week margin materially update the Day Zero question.
Mashhad shows the same low-storage/no-rationing official posture that Tehran had before pressure controls intensified.
The May 10 full-power cutoff date directly defines the next verification window for industrial restrictions.
The social sample supplies bounded negative evidence: scattered anecdotes but no broad coordinated service-disruption wave yet.

operations.reason: v24 adds the water/electricity/service-stress layer on top of v23's May Day managed-grievance layer.
